caption: Paging in one picture: a process is cut into equal pages, memory into equal frames, and any page can sit in any free frame.

subject: os
caption: Paging hardware: the page number *p* indexes the page table to get frame *f*; the offset *d* is copied as-is.

subject: os
caption: Paging example: a 16-byte logical memory with 4-byte pages mapped into a 32-byte physical memory through the page table (5, 6, 1, 2).

subject: os
caption: Paging hardware with a TLB: on a TLB hit the frame number comes straight from the TLB; on a miss the page table is consulted.

subject: os
caption: Valid (v) / invalid (i) bit in the page table: pages 6 and 7 are not part of the process, so touching them traps.

subject: os
caption: Steps in handling a page fault: trap → find the page on disk → load it into a free frame → fix the page table → restart the instruction.

subject: os
caption: Segmentation hardware: the segment number picks a (limit, base) pair; the offset must be less than the limit, then base + offset is the physical address.

subject: os
caption: Page replacement: swap out a victim page, mark it invalid, swap in the needed page, reset the page table.

subject: os
caption: Swapping: a whole process is moved out to secondary memory and another is brought into main memory.

caption: FCFS disk scheduling for queue 98, 183, 37, 122, 14, 124, 65, 67 with head at 53: total head movement 640 cylinders.

subject: os
caption: SSTF on the same queue: always serve the nearest request. Total head movement 236 cylinders.

subject: os
caption: SCAN (elevator) moving towards 0 first: the head sweeps to the end, then reverses. Total 236 cylinders.

subject: os
caption: C-SCAN: sweep one way to the end, jump back to the other end, and continue in the same direction. Total 382 (this figure counts the return jump).

subject: os
caption: C-LOOK: go up only as far as the last request (183), jump back to the lowest pending request (14), and continue upwards.

caption: Demand paging: only pages A, C and F are in memory (valid); the rest stay on disk until they are needed.

caption: Free-frame list before (a) and after (b) a new 4-page process is loaded: pages land in frames 14, 13, 18 and 20.

caption: Many-to-one model: many user threads share one kernel thread, so one blocking call blocks them all.

subject: os
caption: One-to-one model: every user thread gets its own kernel thread (Linux, Windows).

subject: os
caption: Many-to-many model: many user threads are multiplexed onto a smaller or equal number of kernel threads.

subject: os
caption: Bounded buffer: the producer fills slots, the consumer empties them, and the buffer has only *n* slots.

caption: A resource allocation graph with no cycle, so no deadlock. Request edges point P → R; assignment edges point R → P.

subject: os
caption: Top: a RAG with a cycle and a deadlock. Bottom: a RAG with a cycle but no deadlock, because R1 and R2 have spare instances.

subject: os
caption: Safe, unsafe and deadlocked states: deadlock lies inside the unsafe region; staying in safe states guarantees no deadlock.

subject: os
caption: Contiguous allocation: each file occupies consecutive blocks; the directory stores the start block and length.

subject: os
caption: Linked allocation: each block holds a pointer to the next block of the file.

subject: os
caption: Indexed allocation: one index block holds the addresses of all the file's data blocks (file jeep → index block 19).

subject: os
caption: Single-level directory: every file of every user sits in one directory.

subject: os
caption: Two-level directory: a master file directory points to a separate user file directory for each user.

subject: os
caption: Tree-structured directory: directories can contain subdirectories, giving every file a path.

subject: os
caption: Acyclic-graph directory: a file or directory can be shared (linked) from two places, but cycles are not allowed.

subject: os
caption: General-graph directory: links may create cycles, so the OS needs garbage collection and cycle-safe traversal.

caption: Masquerade: Darth sends a message that appears to come from Bob. This is one of the standard security attacks.
